title: heare Phase B-tools — Expand allowed tools beyond bash
source_plan: user request 2026-04-19: 'What if I want an agent to have access to more tools' — Варіант A (expand allowlist).
notes: Currently the Claude SDK is called with allowed_tools=['Bash'] and the IntentQueue accepts only tool='bash'. For voice commands that aren't shell-ish (read a file, edit a file, fetch a URL, web search), Claude either can't act or Gemini forces it through shell. Expand to a five-tool vocabulary: bash, read, write, edit, web_fetch, web_search. Three coordinated changes: queue allowlist, SDK allowed_tools, generator prompt examples. MCP tools are out of scope for this phase.

stories.title: Expand SDK allowed_tools and IntentQueue allowlist
stories.description: Add a configurable list of allowed tools in Settings (default covers bash + the 5 common Claude tools). Thread it into AgentSDKCLI's ClaudeAgentOptions. Sync the queue-side allowlist in src/actions.py so lowercase intent tool names accept the same set.
acceptanceCriteria: src/config.py Settings gains agent_sdk_allowed_tools: list[str] defaulting to ['Bash', 'Read', 'Write', 'Edit', 'WebFetch', 'WebSearch'] (SDK CamelCase).
src/agent_sdk_cli.py _open_client passes settings.agent_sdk_allowed_tools into ClaudeAgentOptions.allowed_tools (no longer hardcoded to ['Bash']).
src/actions.py ALLOWED_TOOLS expands from {'bash'} to {'bash','read','write','edit','web_fetch','web_search'} (intent-side lowercase).

New unit test in tests/test_agent_sdk_cli.py asserts that ClaudeSDKClient is constructed with the extended allowed_tools list by default. Use the existing FakeClient / captured_options pattern (see test_sdk_session_loaded_on_first_call).

New unit tests in tests/test_actions.py verify each new tool (read, write, edit, web_fetch, web_search) is accepted by IntentQueue.submit (tool='bash' still works — existing tests unchanged). A tool outside the set (e.g. 'filesystem') is still rejected.

stories.title: Generator prompt teaches the expanded schema
stories.description: Update prompts/generator.txt INTENTS section: the schema block now lists all 6 allowed tool values; add one concrete positive example per new tool; keep existing bash examples; update negative examples as needed.
acceptanceCriteria: prompts/generator.txt schema block names all six values ('bash', 'read', 'write', 'edit', 'web_fetch', 'web_search') — exact strings checkable in a test.

prompts/generator.txt contains at least one positive example for each new tool: read (e.g. reading a file), write (creating a file with content), edit (modifying a file), web_fetch (fetching a URL), web_search (querying a search engine). All examples in Ukrainian for the reply text.
Negative examples from Phase B retained unchanged.
'If unsure don't emit intent' Ukrainian rule retained.
New unit tests in tests/test_generator_prompt.py: (a) schema names all six tools, (b) at least one positive example present for each of the 5 new tools (substring check per tool keyword).

progress.txt records files touched, the new tool-name vocabulary (lowercase intent side vs CamelCase SDK side), and a live-verify note (say 'знайди в інтернеті що таке Pipecat' → expect intent with tool=web_search).
